problems.description: generator.ts buildSite is a monolith: filesystem traversal, markdown parsing, HTML rendering, and output writes all live in one function, driving the +56 cognitive-complexity delta. It should be split into collect/render/write phases.
cli.ts hand-rolls option parsing with args[++index] and inline process.exitCode mutations inside the parse loop; fragile and not unit-testable as written.

39 convention violations reported (convention score 0.55) for PascalCase classes/interfaces, UPPER_CASE constants, and snake_case functions. Note: the visible code uses camelCase functions and idiomatic TS, so many of these flags appear to be analyzer noise or live in files outside this diff — discrepancy flagged.
cli.ts mixes ESM-style imports with a CommonJS `require.main === module` guard; inconsistent module style that breaks under "type": "module".

The entire seed codebase (93-line Express API with working models/routes/error handling) was deleted with zero reuse, including its seams and the SQLite data layer. Consistent with the greenfield story intent, but it discards prior structure wholesale.
86 AST-counted imports across 8 files for a small SSG is a heavy surface relative to task size; likely inflated by repeated node builtin/type imports but worth a pass.

strengths: Sensible module split (cli entry / generator / parser) with typed public interfaces (BuildOptions, Frontmatter, Page).
Proper scaffolding: package.json with build/test/bin scripts, jest + ts-jest configured with --runInBand, preserving directory structure in URLs via path.sep normalization.
Cross-platform URL derivation and recursive markdown discovery are correct and well-structured.
HTML escaping applied to title/tags/date prevents markup injection into generated pages.
Idempotent builds via rm + mkdir of the output dir before writing.
commit_reviews.summary: A competent greenfield static-site-generator scaffold, but it replaces a clean seed with measurably worse code (SonarQube bugs +1, smells +4, cognitive complexity +56, convention score 0.55), and the 39 convention violations conflict with the visible camelCase code, suggesting analyzer false positives.

problems.description: Hand-rolled template engine partially reimplements two established syntaxes (Handlebars stache + EJS tags, incl. partials/include) via regex, supporting only a subset of each (no conditionals/loops). Divergent behavior from real hbs/ejs will surprise template authors; SonarQube flags cognitive complexity +36.

Supporting two template dialects in one engine doubles surface area (templateNameCandidates probes .hbs/.ejs; renderTemplate branches on both syntaxes). Committing to one syntax or a small library would reduce the maintenance surface.

Raw interpolation ({{{ }}} and <%- %>) emits unescaped output by design; acceptable for template-authored content but should be documented, since layout/partial content is inserted unescaped through the render chain.

No tests added for the new render path (template resolution order, default-template fallback, partials, layout wrapping) despite +146 lines and 7 new functions; the fallback/throw branches (Template not found, ENOENT) are untested.

Repo-wide naming-lint score is 0.55 (PascalCase/UPPER_CASE/snake_case violations across cli.ts, dev-server.ts, generator.ts), but these appear pre-existing: the diff adds +0 classes and only camelCase functions/types, so the introduced lines are idiomatic TS. Flagging discrepancy with the 0.55 measurement.

strengths: CLI parsing mirrors the existing --content/--output option-handling pattern exactly, with the same usage/exit-code behavior.
templateFiles is a faithful mirror of markdownFiles (recursive walk, ENOENT-tolerant), and the feature reuses escapeHtml consistently.
Zero new dependencies — avoids pulling in handlebars/ejs and keeps the SSG self-contained.
Cohesive single-module integration: BuildOptions extended cleanly and non-templated pages keep the existing documentHtml fallback; static analysis reports bugs +0 and duplications 0.0%.
commit_reviews.summary: A cleanly-integrated, pattern-following templating feature (no new deps, bugs +0) that lands a hand-rolled two-syntax template engine with real maintainability cost (+36 cognitive complexity, no tests), against a repo whose 0.55 convention score reflects pre-existing naming-lint debt rather than these new lines.

problems.description: New dev-server module (live reload, WebSocket upgrade path, file serving with path-traversal guard, rebuild coalescing) ships with zero tests despite jest + ts-jest already configured — the rebuild/coalescing and server teardown paths are exactly where regressions will hide.

The option-validation branch `(option !== '--port' || args[0] !== 'serve')` interleaves flag validation with subcommand dispatch, making --port silently rejected under 'build' in a way that reads as a bug; parsing is the convoluted part of an otherwise clean +117-line change.

`server.close()` waits on open keep-alive connections and is not paired with socket tracking or closeAllConnections(), so DevServer.close() can hang on a warm browser tab; ws clients are closed after the server may already be waiting — a classic dev-server teardown race.

DISCREPANCY: the measured convention score (0.55, 39 violations) is largely spurious — cli.ts defines no classes, interfaces, or constants and uses no snake_case, yet is flagged for all of those; the analyzer appears to apply Python naming rules (UPPER_CASE/snake_case) to TypeScript. The actual diff follows existing TS conventions well.

strengths: Reuses buildSite() and BuildOptions rather than reimplementing the generator, so the dev server stays in sync with the real build path.
Live-reload injection happens at serve time only, keeping the static build output clean and the build step side-effect free.
Path traversal is guarded (403 on escape outside outputDir), and the rebuild loop is correctly coalesced via the rebuilding/pending flags.
CLI dispatch mirrors the existing build subcommand shape (usage text, option loop, exit codes), so the surface is consistent.
commit_reviews.summary: A well-integrated dev-server/live-reload feature that extends the existing build pipeline and CLI patterns rather than fighting them, but it ships without tests and a convoluted --port validation branch, while the reported 0.55 convention score is dominated by provably false-positive naming violations.

problems.description: The plugin abstraction leaks: startDevServer reaches into plugin internals (plugin.server) after generator.build() and throws on absence, coupling the SSG lifecycle to a plugin's private state instead of a clean start/close handle returned from the plugin seam.

Net +334/-229 lines, +24 functions, +142 imports and cognitive complexity +24 for a 'refactor' — the new module seams add real indirection/boilerplate; acceptable for extensibility but should be watched if it grows.

Convention score 0.55 with 39 violations (naming: PascalCase classes/interfaces, UPPER_CASE constants, snake_case functions) across cli.ts, dev-server.ts, generator.ts; all must be remediated before this lands in a production surface.
SonarQube +1 smell — a minor code-quality regression introduced alongside the restructuring; no bugs (+0) and no duplication (0.0%) added.

strengths: Cohesive extraction: dev-server.ts shrank 95→16 lines and generator.ts 165→92, with HTTP/websocket/watch/live-reload isolated into plugins/dev-server.
Clean, config-driven plugin seam (Plugin/PluginContext interfaces + configuredPlugins loader) that makes markdown, template, and dev-server concerns independently swappable.
No new bugs and zero duplication introduced while restructuring.
commit_reviews.summary: Solid plugin-architecture refactor that cleanly extracts concerns and shrinks the core files, but lands with a low 0.55 convention score (39 naming violations), added complexity/imports, and a leaky plugin-server lifecycle — with the note that the reported 'Classes should use PascalCase' violations on TS files appear inconsistent with the visible PascalCase code, suggesting the checker may be misapplied.

problems.description: Cache invalidation is incomplete: the template hash covers template files and defaultTemplate only, so changes to plugin code or ssg.config.ts (plugin configuration) won't invalidate cached pages, producing stale output.

Skipped (cached) pages bypass the plugin pipeline — onFile hooks between parsing and rendering never re-run for unchanged pages, so plugins with side effects (asset emission, data mutation) are silently skipped; correctness depends on plugins being pure, which the architecture doesn't guarantee.
SonarQube delta reports +1 new bug in the incremental build path (cache merge/reuse logic).
templateFiles() duplicates the recursive directory-walk logic already present in markdownFiles() instead of generalizing it (duplications +9.4%).
build() cognitive complexity rose +34 with nested cacheUsable/oldCache merge and stale-page-removal conditions, making the hot path harder to reason about.

Convention score is 0.55 with 39 naming violations (PascalCase classes/interfaces, UPPER_CASE constants, snake_case functions); note many flagged files (dev-server.ts) are outside this diff, so a portion is pre-existing.

strengths: The --incremental/--clean CLI flags are wired correctly with subcommand validation (rejected for 'serve'), and the usage string stays in sync with the parser.
Stale-page cleanup removes cached outputs whose source files no longer exist, and a template-hash change triggers a full rebuild — sensible invalidation primitives.
build() now returns BuildStats and the CLI reports built/skipped/time-saved, giving users visible feedback on incremental behavior.
commit_reviews.summary: The commit adds a genuinely useful incremental-build feature that slots into the existing SSG/plugin shape, but it ships with a new SonarQube-detected bug, a large cognitive-complexity jump (+34), 9.4% duplication from re-implementing the walk pattern, and a cache-invalidation gap that can skip plugin hooks and stale on plugin/config changes.

compounding_issues: Frontmatter date bug from S1 never fixed: gray-matter's YAML parser converts `date: 2026-01-02` into a JS Date object, and since the merge is `{...parseYamlBlock(...), ...parsed.data}`, gray-matter's result overwrites the hand-rolled parser on every key collision. The parser test failed from S1 and stayed red through all 5 sessions; the hand-rolled `parseYamlBlock`/`parseScalar` is largely dead code, and the bug is user-visible (dates render as localized Date toString in generated pages).

S4's plugin refactor broke the build: extracting markdown.ts assigned `marked.parse()` (typed `string | Promise<string>` in marked v12) to the `string` field `page.html` (src/plugins/markdown.ts:26). `npm run build` (tsc, run by `prepare`) fails from S4 onward, and ts-jest typechecking then makes the entire generator test suite fail to even execute.

S5 compounded the broken gate: the incremental-build feature (well-designed, with 2 new cache tests) was layered on the S4 break without repair, so its own new tests never run — the suite was already uncompileable.
key_decisions: Discarding the mismatched seed (an Express Todo API) in S1 and rebuilding the static-site generator greenfield as a clean TS project (src/ parser/generator/cli + jest + tsconfig) — the right call that gave S2–S5 a sound foundation.

Hand-rolling a regex-based template engine supporting both Handlebars (`{{}}`, `{{{}}}`, `{{>partial}}`) and EJS (`<%= %>`, `<%- %>`, includes) syntax in S2 rather than adding handlebars/ejs deps — zero-dependency and testable, but shallow (no conditionals/loops) and later copy-pasted nearly verbatim into the S4 template plugin.

S4's plugin architecture (SSG class + Plugin lifecycle hooks onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd + ssg.config.ts loading) — the most consequential architectural step, a genuine extensibility win, but executed without verifying the type-check gate.

S5's content-addressed incremental cache (SHA-256 of source + templates, persisted .ssg-cache.json, template-change invalidation, deleted-page pruning, BuildStats) — a strong cross-cutting decision, though it landed while the build was already red.
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality rose steadily through sessions 1–3: each session added real, tested capability (greenfield scaffold → templating engine with layouts/partials → dev server with watch + live-reload) while keeping `tsc` clean and the generator tests green (only the S1 parser date test was red). The arc peaked architecturally at session 4's plugin refactor, which meaningfully improved extensibility but quietly broke `npm run build` with a marked.parse type error, which also killed the test suite via ts-jest. Session 5 built the well-designed incremental cache on that broken base and never repaired it, so the final state functions at runtime (verified: buildSite works, cache logic is sound) yet fails both the build and test gates — an ambitious, logical progression that ends with its pipelines red.
story_review.summary: A coherent greenfield→feature→integration→refactor→cross-cutting arc with consistently sound engineering instincts, undone by an unverified S4 refactor that broke compilation and a persistent S1 parser bug that was never fixed, leaving the final state failing both `npm run build` and the test suite.
